Research presents conflicting opinions on whether video games are harmful to children's mental health. Some studies indicate video games are harmless for the majority and can provide emotional, social, and learning benefits, even in healthcare settings [d1][d3][d8]. Conversely, other research links excessive or violent game play to increased aggression, anxiety, social dysfunction, and addiction risks, particularly for children with pre-existing vulnerabilities [d2][d4][d5][d6]. The relationship appears complex, with outcomes potentially depending on the child, game type, and amount of play.
